papers.title: Context-Predictive Low-Rank Adaptation for Face Presentation Attack Detection
papers.abstract: Face presentation attack detection requires representations that distinguish physical spoofing cues across changes in acquisition devices, subjects, and attack media. Large visual encoders offer transferable representations, but conventional binary fine-tuning supervises their final decisions without explicitly constraining how local facial evidence is represented under partial observation. We present CP-JEPA, a context-predictive adaptation framework that combines low-rank tuning of a pretrained CLIP image encoder with a joint-embedding predictive objective. A student predicts complete-image teacher features at masked spatial locations, while unmasked classification, masked classification, and prediction consistency retain the connection to the live/spoof task. An exponential-moving-average teacher supplies evolving latent targets. The auxiliary components are used only during training; inference requires only the LoRA-adapted CLIP visual encoder and binary classifier. {We evaluate CP-JEPA under single-source and multi-source OCIM transfer, additional CelebA-Spoof training, transfer to CelebA-Spoof, two-source training, and unseen-attack evaluation on SiW-Mv2.} On the standard OCIM benchmark, CP-JEPA achieves 3.74\% mean HTER and 98.73\% mean AUC. {Single-source evaluation achieves 11.36\% mean HTER across twelve source--target combinations.} With CelebA-Spoof added to the three OCIM training sources, CP-JEPA reduces mean HTER from 3.45\% to 2.35\% and increases mean AUC from 98.68\% to 99.32\%. On SiW-Mv2, it achieves 3.36\% mean HTER across the held-out attack categories. Controlled loss ablations examine the contributions of latent prediction, masked classification, and prediction consistency. The results show that context-predictive adaptation can improve cross-dataset PAD performance, although the gains vary with the training sources and evaluation setting.

papers.title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
papers.abstract: Decoding upper-limb movements from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is an important problem for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but many deep learning models provide limited insight into the brain regions underlying their predictions. We propose a two-branch architecture that combines an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification. The graph branch groups 61 EEG electrodes into anatomically informed regions and learns their spatial relationships, providing a direct representation of the regions emphasized by the model. We evaluate the proposed architecture using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner upper-limb movement dataset. The model achieves a mean F1-score of 0.74 +/- 0.06 across subjects. Beyond classification performance, we analyze the learned graph structure to identify the regions with the strongest connectivity. Across all held-out subjects, the highest connectivity is consistently observed in the Parietal Left Low region, corresponding to electrodes P1 and P3. This region is opposite to the performed right-arm movements and lies within the posterior parietal area previously associated with upper-limb movement processing. These results show that incorporating a region-based graph into the decoder can provide an anatomically interpretable representation while maintaining effective movement classification, offering a practical approach toward more transparent EEG-based BCIs.

papers.title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer
papers.abstract: Accurate future channel state information (CSI) is essential for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication because delays associated with signal propagation, feedback, scheduling, and transceiver reconfiguration can render currently available CSI outdated. However, most existing predictors estimate only the next channel state and obtain multi-step forecasts through recursive rollout, which causes prediction errors to accumulate as the multipath structure evolves. The scarcity of sea-trial measurements further limits reliable model training. To address these challenges, we propose LLM4UACP, a dual-domain, structure-preserving framework that adapts a pretrained Transformer for few-shot multi-step UWA channel prediction. LLM4UACP extracts complementary features from the channel impulse response (CIR) and channel frequency response (CFR), aligns them through Fourier-consistent fusion, and encodes the fused representation as delay-time tokens. A pretrained Transformer with a frozen backbone is adapted through Butterfly Orthogonal Fine-tuning to jointly predict multiple future CIRs in a single forward pass, thereby avoiding the error accumulation associated with recursive prediction. Experiments on the measured SO-06 and SO-07 channels show that LLM4UACP achieves normalized mean squared error (NMSE) values of 0.0411 and 0.0399, corresponding to reductions of 88.53% and 85.15%, respectively, relative to the most recent baseline. With only 0.11M trainable parameters, LLM4UACP maintains robust performance across varying prediction horizons and observation-window lengths, limited-data settings, and cross-dataset transfer scenarios.

papers.title: Risk-Aware Joint Inference and Resource Control for Physical AI in 6G Networks
papers.abstract: Wireless edge inference enables Physical-AI devices to execute edge-inferred actions using transmitted sensory inputs. Since the risk of incorrect actions vary across observations and tasks, the associated uplink transmission of sensory inputs requires different levels of wireless reliability. For instance, applying a fixed signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) requirement can overprovision low-risk tasks while underprovisioning high-risk ones. Therefore, we propose risk-aware control for edge inference (RACE), which maps predicted action-failure probability and task criticality to adaptive SINR targets and combines them with deadline-derived SINR requirements. A slow-timescale large language model (LLM) proposes task requirements for deterministic validation, while a fast hybrid actor selects inference configurations and transmit power levels, complemented by analytical receive beamforming and finite power restoration. Simulations show $11\%$ improvement in the average accuracy-latency-energy objective over fixed-high-SINR control, with near-zero constraint outage.

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Spectrum Data Obfuscation in Next-Generation Spectrum Coexistence Systems
papers.abstract: In spectrum coexistence systems, the primary user (PU) activity must be partially disclosed for interference avoidance and coordination, while the exact spectrum occupancy information is often restricted due to security and regulatory constraints. To this end, subset-based disclosures can be employed in which the true frequency is included while ambiguity is introduced. This paper shows that naive randomized subset disclosures remain highly vulnerable to information leakage through inference, as temporal structure can be exploited to recover spectrum usage information. Under Markovian dynamics of the PU's spectrum usage, hidden Markov model (HMM) filtering with online learning is applied, while under periodic dynamics, period and phase estimations with phase-aligned statistics are used for inference. To address this vulnerability, structure-aware obfuscation strategies are introduced. For Markovian dynamics, history-based and belief-based schemes are designed to induce model mismatch and limit posterior concentration, while for periodic dynamics, cycle-dominance and decoy-based schemes are designed to manipulate phase-wise statistics and bias the inference process. These obfuscation schemes significantly hinder inference of spectrum information and offer principled disclosure solutions for spectrum coexistence systems.

papers.title: The BEATS Dataset: Towards Understanding Music-Physiology Dynamics in Real-World Scenarios
papers.abstract: We introduce the BEATS dataset, a robust compilation of psycho-physiological data collected in the wild from 30 participants while they listened to curated playlists intended to promote well-being. An acronym for Biomarkers, Experience and Affect from Therapeutic Soundscapes, the BEATS dataset aims to support research on wellbeing, music psychology, affective computing and signal processing. More specifically, this dataset includes: (1) sensor data collected during music listening sessions using a research-grade wearable device in free-movement environments; (2) music listening activity records, stimulus metadata, acoustic features, and self-reports associated with the listening sessions (3) individual characteristics, such as demographics, music preference, musical skills, and personality traits; and (4) self-reported psychological measures before and after their experimental participation spanning for a number of weeks. By situating data collection outside of lab settings, the BEATS dataset offers the opportunity to study real-world music-listening scenarios, allowing for a richer exploration of the physiological, subjective and therapeutic effects of music under real-world conditions.

papers.title: Re-evaluating Heart Rate Variability Biomarkers for Glucose Sensing: The Impact of Age Normalisation and Subject-Independent Validation
papers.abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals may indicate glycemic status, but prior studies often combine distinct glucose targets and use validation strategies vulnerable to data leakage. Since HRV declines with age, aging may be confounded with diabetes-related autonomic dysfunction. We tested whether age-dependent HRV normalisation improves glycemic estimation. We analysed ECG features from 43 male patients with type 2 diabetes. Outcomes were glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c; n=29) and fasting blood glucose (FBG; n=38). We used leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, with feature selection and standardisation within each training fold. We compared 20 machine-learning algorithms, six age-adjustment methods, and 20 normalisation parameter combinations. Validation included 500 permutations and bootstrap confidence intervals. Extra Trees regression performed best: R2=0.222 (r=0.476, p=0.009) for HbA1c and R2=0.086 (r=0.344, p=0.034) for FBG. Mean absolute errors were 1.18 percentage points and 2.27 mmol/L, respectively. Permutation testing supported both associations (p=0.002). Contrary to our hypothesis, no age-adjustment method or parameter combination improved performance. Tree ensembles retained positive performance under strict validation, whereas linear models had negative R2 values; neural networks performed poorly. Strict within-fold preprocessing materially changed model performance and revealed potential inflation from conventional validation. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were [0.13, 0.82] for HbA1c R2 and [0.10, 0.72] for FBG R2. Although findings support HRV-glycemic associations, performance remains insufficient for standalone clinical use. The study highlights the importance of separating glycemic targets, subject-independent validation, within-fold preprocessing, and comprehensive baselines in non-invasive glycemic monitoring research.

papers.title: A Foundation Model for Electrodermal Activity Data
papers.abstract: Foundation models have recently extended beyond natural language and vision to time-series domains, including physiological signals. Yet developing foundation models for electrodermal activity (EDA) remains hindered by the absence of large-scale, curated, openly accessible datasets. EDA reflects sympathetic activity and is widely used to infer cognitive load, stress, and engagement. However, few wearable devices feature EDA sensing, and the only large-scale EDA archive to date is proprietary. To address this gap, we compile EDAMAME, a collection of EDA traces from 29 public datasets comprising approximately 23,000 hours of data from 731 users. Using this collection, we train UME, the first foundation model for EDA. As a frozen feature extractor, UME outperforms generic handcrafted features and matches generalist time-series foundation models while requiring 20x fewer computational resources; fine-tuning on the downstream tasks further yields additional performance gains in most experiments. UME also generalizes to EDA from two devices unseen during training. We further show that UME's performance improves as the amount of pretraining data grows, underscoring the importance of large-scale data for effective foundation models. Our findings highlight intrinsic challenges of EDA signals, revealing future research opportunities. We share EDAMAME under tiered access and also release model weights and code.

papers.title: Reduced-Complexity WMMSE Approach for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems With Finite-Capacity Fronthaul Links
papers.abstract: We propose a reduced-complexity weighted minimum mean squared error (R-WMMSE) framework for cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems with finite-capacity fronthaul links. To maximize the system capacity, we need to jointly design beamforming vectors at distributed access points (APs) and fronthaul quantization noise covariances. Such a task would be addressed using conventional WMMSE algorithms and their variants. However, existing WMMSE-based methods either assume ideal infinite-capacity fronthaul links or incur high computational complexity when jointly optimizing the network-wide beamforming and fronthaul compression variables. To this end, the proposed method jointly optimizes beamforming and fronthaul compression by leveraging a sequential per-AP optimization strategy. Since each subproblem is efficiently solved via Lagrangian duality with closed-form updates, the overall computational complexity can be significantly reduced compared to the conventional WMMSE method. To further reduce hardware cost, we extend the R-WMMSE framework to hybrid analog-digital beamforming systems, tackling the joint design of digital beamforming, fronthaul compression, and analog beamforming. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance nearly identical to that of the conventional WMMSE while reducing the runtime by over 99%.

papers.title: Multimodal Semantic Communication using Shared and Unique Representation Decomposition
papers.abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm for bandwidth-constrained mobile and vehicular networks. This paper proposes a unified representation learning framework for multimodal SemCom (MSC), which encodes heterogeneous data into a compact semantic space for efficient transmission and source recovery. The framework addresses the multimodal semantic representation gap, which arises when at least one modality contains semantic information that cannot be fully inferred from the other. To preserve this information for reconstruction, the framework decomposes each representation into shared and modality-specific components. We formulate a mutual information objective for source reconstruction, cross-modal alignment of the shared components, and decoupling of the shared and modality-specific components. To enhance transmission efficiency, we introduce a shared knowledge base implemented as a compact codebook of semantic vectors learned during training. The shared components are transmitted digitally as codebook indices, while the modality-specific components are sent in analog form. We apply knowledge distillation during training, using a pretrained vision foundation model to guide the learning of quantized shared features. On image--text pairs over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Extended Vehicular A (EVA) channels, the proposed framework improves image reconstruction over conventional separate source-channel coding (SSCC) and representative multimodal and unimodal SemCom systems. Further evaluations show gradual degradation under channel-estimation mismatch, complementary effects of alignment, decoupling, and knowledge distillation on the shared representation, and alignment of shared features across modalities with separation of the modality-specific features.

papers.title: VR-Net: Subarray-Level Inter-Cell Coordination for Multi-Cell XL-MIMO under Near-Field Spatial Non-Stationarity
papers.abstract: Spatial non-stationarity in multi-cell extremely large-scale MIMO (XL-MIMO) confines each user to a visibility region (VR) of each array. VR-Net exploits these regions for subarray-level coordinated beamforming. A base-station (BS)-indexed conflict graph identifies overlapping VRs; gain-based association and a masked multi-cell weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) iteration restrict beam design and channel state information (CSI) uploads to the relevant subarray blocks. We establish conditions for exact per-cell decoupling, derive the expected CSI loads, bound the loss of designing on the VR-gated channel and the loss of the support constraint, and characterize single-edge visibility contrast through a closed-form Fresnel transition width. Simulations use a 3GPP TR 38.901 Release-19-based near-field UMi channel with modular facade arrays and pre-registered criteria. At a 30 dB threshold, VR-Net retains at least 99.6% of the full-aperture WMMSE sum rate in every tested setting while uploading 10-39% fewer complex CSI entries. It gains up to 3.5 bit/s/Hz over an all-user adaptation of the multi-cell scheme of P\'erez-Ad\'an et al. at moderate power and dense load, and inter-cell coordination adds up to 33% over per-cell design.

papers.title: Optimization of Finite Alphabet Message Passing Decoding on Fully Node-Parallel Architectures for 5G LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel design method for the lookup tables (LUTs) of the minimum reconstruction, computation, and quantization (min-RCQ) LDPC code decoding algorithm. The proposed design method uses Bayesian optimization and samples from a subspace of the design space. The novel design method does not require knowledge about the channel or the modulation format and uses the frame error rate (FER) as loss function. The design method is applicable to irregular low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with puncturing and shortening. Furthermore, the design method creates a set of iteration-agnostic LUTs that can be used over all iterations, which makes this approach suitable for fully node-parallel decoder architectures. We show that our proposed approach achieves a 38.6 % better energy efficiency than a state-of-the-art normalized min-sum (NMS) decoder without loss in error correction performance.

papers.title: Subject-Held-Out Evaluation of Deep Ground Reaction Force Estimators Across Two Laboratories: Leakage and Cross-Laboratory Transfer
papers.abstract: Deep networks that estimate ground reaction forces and centers of pressure from motion-capture markers are validated within one laboratory, in a seldom-stated coordinate frame, and sometimes with trial-level splits that put the same person in the training and the test set. We measured what each practice costs, and whether such models transfer between laboratories. Three sequence models (convolutional, convolutional-recurrent, and convolutional-transformer) were evaluated on two independent datasets, locomotion (6 subjects) and occupational patient handling (10 subjects), under one pipeline, one tuning procedure, three seeds, and four protocols: trial-level split, leave-one-subject-out, pooled two-laboratory training with matched held-out subjects, and cross-laboratory transfer. At a fixed configuration, trial-level splits overstated the subject-held-out coefficient of determination by +0.040 to +0.194; on occupational data the overstatement exceeded every difference between architectures. With subjects held out, the three models reached values between 0.583 and 0.804; the leader differed between datasets, and gaps lay within subject-to-subject variability. Pooling the laboratories changed neither dataset on matched subjects. Transfer between laboratories was below chance in both directions, including the vertical force, which no in-plane rotation can affect. Leaving force targets in the plate frame while inputs were heading-aligned cost 0.57 of locomotion anteroposterior-force explained variance, enough to make that force look hardest; a Newton's-law correlation detected the mismatch before training. Split protocol and target frame changed reported accuracy more than architecture did. Learned force estimators should be validated with subjects held out, checked for frame consistency before training, and tested across laboratories before deployment claims are made.

papers.title: An $O(L^3)$ Spherical Harmonic Transform on $L^2$ Samples
papers.abstract: For the representation of signals on the sphere band-limited at $L$ using the optimal number of samples, $L^2$, equal to the number of degrees of freedom in harmonic space and placed on $L$ iso-latitude rings, we develop a spherical harmonic transform (SHT) that is theoretically exact, requires no solution of linear systems and no precomputation beyond the placement of the rings, and has complexity $O(L^3)$. The transform rests on the observation that, for each order $m$, the samples on the rings that resolve order $m$ are a complete set of samples for the order-$m$ profile of the signal, so that its values on the remaining rings follow from a closed-form Lagrange basis, the sampling functions of order $m$. We prove that the proposed optimal-dimensionality SHT (OSHT) recovers every band-limited signal exactly in exact arithmetic, so that the $L^2$ samples admit a sampling theorem in the collocation sense. For the final harmonic analysis we give two exact back-ends: Gauss-Legendre quadrature of the interpolated profiles and the algorithm of the equiangular sampling theorem, which applies without change because the rings coincide with its grid. We identify the amplification constant that governs numerical error, show that it replaces the condition number used previously for the placement of rings, propose a placement that minimizes it, and give an error propagation model that explains the growth of error with the band-limit. A multi-pass refinement converges in two passes to the rounding floor of the samples. We also describe a stable log-domain evaluation of the sampling functions, a rescaled Legendre recurrence, and a forbidden-region skipping rule that halves the cost of the elimination. Numerical experiments up to $L=2048$ characterize the accuracy, measured by the maximum and mean coefficient errors and the signal-to-noise ratio, the stability and the computation time.

papers.title: Optimized Mirabbasi-Martin Pulse Shaping Filter for Higher-Order Modulation in Zak-OTFS
papers.abstract: The performance of Zak-OTFS modulation depends critically on the delay-Doppler (DD) domain pulse shaping filter, which must support both accurate channel estimation and reliable data detection. Filters reported in the Zak-OTFS literature fall short in bit error rate (BER) performance for higher-order modulation due to sensitivity to model-free channel estimation errors and pilot-data interference. Motivated by this, in this paper, we introduce a separable two-dimensional Mirabbasi-Martin (MM) filter for Zak-OTFS and propose a filter coefficient optimization framework that minimizes the aggregate sidelobe energy while preserving the compact structure of the MM prototype. By trading exact Nyquist nulls for high localization, the optimized MM filter exhibits no sidelobes with the narrowest $-40$ dB DD domain pulsewidth compared to sinc, Gaussian, and GS pulses. This compactness of the optimized filter tightly confines the pilot energy within the pilot region of the embedded frame, ensuring that the full response is captured for model-free channel estimation while significantly reducing pilot-data interference. This yields both an improved estimation performance and a significantly improved BER performance for higher-order QAM. For the proposed filter, we derive closed-form expressions for the effective DD domain channel and the covariance of the receive-filtered noise, which drastically reduce simulation run times. Our simulation results demonstrate that the optimized MM filter achieves significantly better uncoded/coded BER performance for higher-order QAM compared to that of sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters. For example, for 64-QAM with M=32, N=48, rate-1/2 convolutional code, and TDL-A channel model with fractional DDs, the optimized MM filter achieves a coded BER of 3x10^{-4} at an E_b/N_0 of 40 dB, while the sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters exhibit error floors above 10^{-2}.

papers.title: ScrewSense: Mapping the Invisible - Anomaly Detection and Error Classification in Screwdriving Processes
papers.abstract: The growing volume of process data generated by screwdriving systems, combined with advancements in computing power, data storage, and algorithms, is facilitating the application of artificial intelligence in this field. Accurately detecting and classifying screwdriving errors is crucial for ensuring product quality, avoiding costly rework in manufacturing, and supporting sustainability by facilitating the maintenance, reuse, and recycling of screw-connected products. In this context, machine learning approaches offer a promising alternative to traditional monitoring techniques, such as window-based methods or envelope curves. This study examines the use of deep learning techniques for anomaly detection and error classification in screwdriving processes. The data corpus consists of multivariate time series capturing process parameters, such as torque and rotation angle. For anomaly detection, the embedding space of a vector quantized variational autoencoder was analyzed. In terms of error classification, four different model architectures were evaluated. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of anomaly detection and confirm that deep learning models can distinguish between multiple error categories beyond traditional binary classification. This extends the capabilities of conventional monitoring approaches, achieving accuracies of up to 100%. Additionally, real-world data material was examined in order to further demonstrate model robustness. Overall the results indicate strong generalization capability and highlight the practical potential of the developed models for use in industrial screwdriving processes, eliminating the need for expert knowledge in error identification and significantly reducing manual effort and analysis time.

papers.title: Capacity-Constrained Delayed Feedback for Online Conformal Risk Control
papers.abstract: Online conformal risk control (OCRC) enables reliable uncertainty quantification in machine learning by converting model outputs into prediction sets with long-term risk guarantees. These guarantees, however, hinge on the assumption that the loss of each round is revealed immediately and losslessly. In practice, feedback may be delayed, and limited resources may prevent tracking all pending predictions, causing some feedback to be lost. To address this challenge, we develop capacity-aware OCRC (CA-OCRC), a framework that jointly determines how to allocate limited tracking feedback capacity and how to construct prediction sets. CA-OCRC is based on a randomized tracking policy that samples a proxy delay to decide whether, and for how long, feedback for the current round is tracked. CA-OCRC updates the prediction sets via inverse probability weighting, compensating for the possibility of feedback lost due to delays and limited tracking capacity. We analyze risk bounds for both arbitrary and stochastic delays, revealing a trade-off between receiving more feedback and avoiding capacity saturation. Building on these bounds, we optimize the proxy delay distribution, showing scaling laws for the tracking capacity that ensure the same long-term risk as OCRC with unlimited feedback. Experiments on medical imaging, natural language processing, computer vision, and wireless communications show the effectiveness of CA-OCRC as compared to existing OCRC mechanisms.

papers.title: Learning Mixtures of Exponential Family
papers.abstract: Motivated by causal inference and physical computing systems, we consider the problem of learning mixture of two bounded-support exponential-family distributions with a shared interaction parameter matrix and mixture component-specific linear parameter vectors. The unknown sequence of component labels belongs to a known structured class. We propose an estimator based on a convex loss that avoids the log-partition function; for each fixed label assignment, estimation is a convex optimization problem. We show that the conditional population loss uniquely identifies the interaction matrix and the linear parameter attached to each sample. For a global empirical minimizer, we establish finite-sample bounds on the interaction error in Frobenius norm and the average squared linear-parameter error. The bounds depend on the logarithm of the number of admissible label assignments, and, for fixed dimension and model bounds, imply consistency when this complexity grows sublinearly with sample size. Additional occupancy and separation conditions yield component and label recovery.

papers.title: Reliable Near-Field Source Enumeration and Positioning Informed by Two-Stage MUSIC
papers.abstract: Accurate and reliable near-field multi-source localization is essential for location-aware processing in future wireless systems. However, coherent multipath propagation complicates the direct recovery of line-of-sight (LoS) source positions, while existing estimation methods generally lack explicit control of the risk of source underestimation and positioning uncertainty. In this paper, we investigate reliable source enumeration and positioning in near-field coherent multipath environments. Specifically, we develop a conformal risk control (CRC) based source enumeration scheme that calibrates the penalty coefficient of an eigenvalue-based criterion to control the expected miss-detection ratio at a prescribed level. We further propose MUSIC-Net, a model-based deep learning framework informed by two-stage MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC), which learns the LoS-related subspace and surrogate distances through subspace-distance-based training, thereby enabling direct source positioning without estimating non-line-of-sight (NLoS) path parameters or performing subsequent path association. To quantify the uncertainty of the estimated positions, we develop a split conformal prediction (SCP) based calibration method that constructs angle-range predicted regions with finite-sample simultaneous coverage guarantees. Numerical results show that the proposed framework effectively controls the risk of source underestimation, while providing improved positioning accuracy with tighter predicted regions than benchmarks given the same target coverage levels.

papers.title: Rule-Sensitive Sensor Participation in Distributed Detection with Prescribed Boolean Fusion Rules
papers.abstract: We study distributed binary detection when the fusion node must implement a prescribed Boolean decision rule. Under conditionally independent Bernoulli observations, we derive a signed-influence path identity valid for arbitrary Boolean rules; for monotone rules, it reduces to an exact Russo--Margulis representation in terms of coordinate influences. The identity yields rule-sensitive necessary conditions for a target Bayes error and an influence-weighted Kullback--Leibler feasibility bound. We then connect Boolean relevance to exact rule implementation and derive lower bounds on the number of sensors that must participate, including a heterogeneous bound based on the ordered per-sensor hypothesis separations. Numerical and Monte Carlo results illustrate both the tightening provided by the heterogeneous participation bound and the performance penalty that can arise when a prescribed fusion rule is retained instead of optimal likelihood-ratio fusion.

papers.title: Flexible Intelligent Metasurfaces for Enhancing Secure MISO Communications
papers.abstract: This letter investigates flexible intelligent metasurface (FIM)-aided secure multiple-input single-output (MISO) communications in the presence of a multi-antenna eavesdropper. By exploiting the morphing capability of the FIM, the transmit array geometry can be dynamically reconfigured to reshape the legitimate and eavesdropping channels. We formulate a secrecy rate maximization (SRM) problem by jointly optimizing the transmit covariance matrix and the FIM surface shape. For a given FIM surface shape, the optimal transmit covariance matrix is shown to be rank one and is obtained in closed form from the dominant generalized eigenvector. For a fixed transmit covariance matrix, a projected gradient ascent (PGA) method is developed to optimize the FIM shape. Based on these two subproblems, a block coordinate ascent (BCA) algorithm is proposed. Moreover, for the special line-of-sight (LoS) scenario, we derive a globally optimal closed-form joint transmit covariance matrix and FIM surface shape design under a sufficient morphing-range condition. Numerical results demonstrate that FIM effectively improves the secrecy rate over a conventional rigid antenna array (RAA). Moreover, FIM achieves a transmit-power saving of about 2.5 dB compared with the RAA benchmark at the same secrecy rate.

papers.title: Measurement-Calibrated Synthetic Pretraining for Rapid Adaptation of UAV Channel Predictors
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) links can change faster than route-specific channel data can be collected, so a channel predictor must often be adapted from only a short target-flight calibration segment. This paper studies measurement-calibrated synthetic pretraining as an offline source prior for rapid adaptation of channel state information (CSI) predictors. The synthetic source is calibrated to flight-only power evolution, temporal shape variation, frequency selectivity, and phase disturbance, and is then combined with measured source-flight fine-tuning before target-flight adaptation. Under chronological held-out flight splits, synthetic-to-real (S2R) fine-tuning reduces the measured-data budget needed to reach useful prediction in the low-data regime. For 50 ms-ahead prediction, it crosses a latest-channel-estimate persistence baseline with 50 measured training windows, roughly 0.5 s of 10 ms-spaced supervised windows, whereas training from scratch requires 600 windows. A target-prefix adaptation study further shows that a lightweight gated recurrent unit predictor can reuse the pretrained source prior with one prediction-layer update epoch, positioning measurement-calibrated synthetic pretraining as a reusable prior for scarce target-flight measurements.

papers.title: ISAC with Backscattering RFID Tags: Beamforming and Codebook Design
papers.abstract: This paper explores an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system with backscattering radio frequency identification (RFID) tags. In this setup, an access point employs communication beams to serve communication users while leveraging a sensing beam to interrogate RFID tags. Under the total transmit power constraint of the system, our objective is to design a joint sensing and communication beamforming codebook by considering the tag interrogation and communication requirements. To lay a foundation for the codebook design problem, we first study the beamforming design problem in the single-tag scenario and investigate two approaches: a two-stage zero-forcing-based design with optimized power allocation and a joint beamforming design that minimizes the total transmit power. Extending our study to the multi-tag scenario, we propose a site-specific beamforming codebook design. The proposed approach partitions the region of interest into angular sectors and jointly optimizes the sensing and communication beams for each sector. The simulation results show that the proposed beamforming designs can effectively mitigate the mutual interference between sensing and communication functionalities, thus enhancing the interrogation range of the tags while minimizing transmit power. Also, the efficacy of the proposed site-specific codebook design has been demonstrated in terms of interrogation success rate, offering a promising approach for ISAC backscattering systems.

papers.title: Equation-Free Digital Twins for Nonlinear Structural Dynamics
papers.abstract: Monitoring floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) under stochastic excitation and sensor failure requires computationally efficient and physically interpretable estimators. This paper introduces an equation-free, output-only digital twin framework combining Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (Hankel-DMD), sparse-sensor reconstruction, and a stochastic Kalman extension. A sufficient identifiability condition is derived for modal amplitudes recovered from delay-embedded measurements, while Tikhonov regularization addresses ill-conditioned sensor layouts. Correlation-domain identification improves damping estimates under stochastic forcing and distinguishes structural modes from rotor harmonics. The framework is validated using OpenFAST simulations of an NREL 5-MW spar turbine and experimental basin-test measurements from a 1:70-scale IEA 15-MW semi-submersible. In simulations, the identified tower modes agree with established operational modal analysis methods (MAC at least 0.99), while the Kalman estimator achieves R-squared values of 0.91 to 0.99 under severe sensor sparsity. Experimental results identify tower modes at 0.430 and 0.415 Hz with MAC of 1.00 against SSI-COV and reconstruct tower-base bending moments on unseen runs with R-squared values of 0.83 to 0.89 using three of four sensors. The framework provides a computationally efficient, sensor-failure-resilient structural-state estimation layer for digital twins.

papers.title: Deep Unrolling of Lanczos-based Laplacian Eigensolver for Crop Classification in Satellite Images
papers.abstract: Per-pixel crop classification in satellite images is an important pre-processing step in remote crop monitoring. Leveraging progress in signed graph signal processing, we build an interpretable and lightweight neural network for binary crop classification (e.g., corn versus non-corn) in two stages: i) learn a signed graph from data, and ii) unroll a Lanczos-based eigensolver to compute the eigenvector $\u_1$ associated with the smallest eigenvalue of a hybrid graph Laplacian $\cL$ for spectral clustering. Specifically, we first construct a near-balanced signed graph $\cG^s$, where signed edge weights $w_{i,j}\in(-1,1)$ are computed from learned feature distances $d_{i,j}$ via a hyperbolic tangent mapping. Given $\cG^s$, we estimate $\u_1$ by unrolling the Lanczos algorithm and use $\mathrm{sign}(\u_1)$ for binary classification. Mathematically, we develop a theorem establishing conditions under which $\u_1$ can be well approximated after finite Lanczos iterations. Motivated by this theorem, we relax the classical Lanczos orthogonality constraints during unrolling and optimize end-to-end classification performance while promoting the derived conditions for accurate eigenvector approximation. Experiments on real-world Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel imagery show classification performance comparable to state-of-the-art deep learning models while reducing parameters by up to two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Joint Beamforming and Duplex-Mode Segment Selection for Secure Uplink Transmission in Pinching Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) have recently emerged as a promising architecture for reconfigurable, flexible and proximity-driven signal delivery. In this paper, we propose a segmented waveguide-based PASS architecture for enabling secure uplink communications, where each segment activates at most one pinching antenna (PA), which inherently eliminates the inter-antenna re-radiation effect and yields a tractable uplink signal model. To protect the uplink transmission against eavesdropping, the base station (BS) injects artificial noise (AN) toward the eavesdroppers via selected downlink segments using a duplex-mode segment selection mechanism, which dynamically configures each segment for either uplink reception or downlink AN transmission through switch-controlled fiber connections. We formulate the secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) that jointly optimizes the receive beamforming vector, AN covariance, user transmit power, pinching antenna positions, and duplex-mode segment assignment. Given the non-convex and combinatorial nature of the problem, we develop an efficient alternating optimization (AO) framework, where the resulting subproblems are solved using the Dinkelbach method combined with successive convex approximation (SCA) and penalty-based relaxation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of SEE and robustness against waveguide attenuation. Moreover, AN effectively suppresses information leakage, while PA mobility, duplex-mode segment allocation, and waveguide segmentation further improve secrecy performance through flexible positioning and reduced in-waveguide propagation loss.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of Quantization-Aware Neural Channel Estimation with Low-Precision Inference
papers.abstract: Neural channel estimators can improve radio performance of 5G receivers, but real-time deployment in the radio access network (RAN) imposes strict latency and power budgets. Prior studies of quantized neural channel estimators assess this cost through mean-squared error or analytic operation counts. In this paper, we train a 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) channel estimator for the 5G NR physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) with INT8 and FP8 quantization-aware training (QAT), and we evaluate its radio performance together with its latency, power, and energy on an NVIDIA H100 GPU. On TDL-A and TDL-C channels at user equipment (UE) speeds up to 35 m/s, both 8-bit models stay within 0.025 dB of FP32 at 10% block error rate (BLER). At batch size 128, INT8 reduces the latency by 16%, the incremental GPU power by 33%, and the energy per query by 26%, compared with 6%, 26%, and 21% for FP8. INT8 is therefore the preferred format.

papers.title: Full-Duplex Communication for Pinching Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: This paper investigates multiuser full-duplex (FD) communication assisted by a multiwaveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) where each dielectric waveguide can be dynamically configured to operate in either downlink transmission or uplink reception mode. We develop a channel model that accounts for in-waveguide power attenuation and cumulative pinching antenna (PA)-induced phase shift. Building on this model, we jointly optimize the waveguide modes, PA locations, PA radiation/collection coefficients, downlink beamformers, uplink receive combiners, and uplink transmit powers to maximize the downlink weighted sum-rate (WSR) subject to uplink quality-of-service (QoS) requirements and power constraints. To tackle the resulting mixed-integer nonconvex resource allocation problem, we propose a low-complexity hierarchical block coordinate descent algorithm that capitalizes on weighted minimum mean-square error, fractional programming, majorization-minimization, and the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to obtain a high-quality suboptimal solution. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed FD-PASS outperforms an FD base station equipped with fixed antennas and exhibits greater robustness against residual self-interference. Moreover, ignoring cumulative PA-induced phase shifts can produce QoS-infeasible designs.

papers.title: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing With Pre-Chirp Spreading Index Modulation: A CSI-Driven Secure Transmission Framework
papers.abstract: The flexible configurability of pre-chirp parameters in affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) provides new degrees of freedom for designing covert communication mechanisms. Leveraging this property, this paper proposes a covert AFDM pre-chirp spreading index modulation (IM) framework referred to as AFDM-PCS-IM, tailored for high-mobility scenarios. Specifically, an orthogonal pre-chirp parameter codebook is constructed by exploiting the tunability of the pre-chirp parameters. To enhance covertness, the legitimate channel state information (CSI) is utilized to generate controlled perturbations that encrypt the codebook, thereby tightly coupling the modulation structure with instantaneous channel characteristics. The encrypted pre-chirp codebook is then employed as an IM dimension for information transmission, where the index bits are conveyed through the selection of pre-chirp parameter sequences. Since eavesdroppers cannot obtain consistent CSI, they are unable to reconstruct the encrypted codebook and thus cannot reliably recover any useful information. Moreover, to address channel estimation errors inherent in practical communication environments, a noise-aware CSI quantizer is further introduced to improve robustness under imperfect CSI conditions. Finally, a low-complexity two-layer message passing detector with Walsh code constraints (TLMP-WC) is developed to enable efficient large-scale data detection while simultaneously enhancing the detection reliability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AFDM-PCS-IM framework with the TLMP-WC detector achieves superior covertness, improved bit error rate (BER) performance, and reduced computational complexity compared with the state-of-the-art schemes.

papers.title: Multi-Band Indoor MIMO Channel Measurements Across Sub-6 GHz, Mid-Band and mmWave: Comparing 2.55 GHz, 12.75 GHz and 25.5 GHz
papers.abstract: Future wireless systems for indoor applications are expected to extend their operating frequencies from sub-6 GHz to mid-band and millimeter wave (mmWave) frequencies to support higher data rates. To characterize the frequency-dependent propagation behavior across these bands, multi-band channel measurements are essential. In this work, we conduct double-directional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel measurements in an indoor environment to enable a consistent comparison across three frequency bands. Measurements are performed using a 16x16 MIMO configuration at center frequencies of 2.55 GHz, 12.75 GHz and 25.5 GHz, covering both line-of-sight (LOS) and obstructed line-of-sight (OLOS) conditions. The measured channels are processed using the space-alternating generalized expectation maximization (SAGE) algorithm to extract multipath parameters, which are subsequently used to characterize the angular power distributions across the three frequency bands. The results show substantial angular-domain similarity across all three bands in both LOS and OLOS conditions, while also highlighting frequency-dependent variations.
